subject: Sequencing MAP & Eval: pivoting orderform/DPA path for MedAlign pilot
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sequencing MAP & Eval: pivoting orderform/DPA path for MedAlign pilot

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion I attached a draft MAP (MedAlign_MAP_v3.xlsx) that pulls together the evaluation milestones, security intake steps, and the signing dependencies we expect between the MSA, DPA, and order form. High level asks:

- Confirm whether MedAlign requires a fully executed DPA before the order form is countersigned, or whether you can accept an order form with a conditional acceptance clause while DPA negotiation runs in parallel.
- Confirm security evidence request: SOC 2 + summary + any region-specific data residency constraints.
- Approve the pilot window: 2025-11-03 -> 2025-11-24 (3 weeks). We proposed a pilot go/no-go gate on 2025-11-24 tied to acceptance criteria in the MAP.

Suggested sequencing in the draft MAP:
1) Security intake & SOC2 evidence (Week 0–1) — procurement/legal review starts in parallel.
2) DPA redline cycle (Week 1–3) — target 10 business days for redlines.
3) Order form signature (Week 2) — we can either sign order form subject to DPA completion or wait until DPA is final depending on your procurement rules.
4) Pilot kickoff (Day after order form signature) — unless you require the DPA final before any data processing.

I've also attached the Redwood guidance doc on MSA/DPA granularity (Redwood_MSA_DPA_granularity.pdf) and a clean orderform draft (orderform-draft-2.docx).

If you prefer, we can propose a single-line conditional clause to include in the order form that explicitly ties the purchase effective date to DPA execution (we've used this with several customers to unblock pilots while legal finishes the DPA).

Would love to get your preferred ordering (DPA first vs parallel) and any procurement deadlines on your side so we can lock dates in the MAP.

Thanks —
Hannah

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the materials and the clear MAP. A couple of clarifications from procurement/legal here at MedAlign:

1) Our baseline policy is that any vendor processing PHI or subject to data residency rules needs a fully executed DPA before invoice/payment triggers. We are not running PHI for this pilot, but do have PII and some limited patient identifiers.
2) Procurement would prefer the DPA in signed form prior to countersigning the order form. That said, if Redwood can accept a conditional order form that explicitly states the order is contingent on DPA execution and that no customer data will be ingested until the DPA is effective, our team may accept signing the order form sooner to secure the pilot window.
3) Please send the SOC 2 report and the security questionnaire responses. I attached our procurement intake form for your team to fill (medalign_procurement_intake.pdf).

We can commit to a 2-week legal review for the DPA if Redwood can provide a redline-friendly version and a short rationale for any nonstandard clauses. Our internal legal lead (Tom) is copied.

Elena Ruiz
Director, Partnerships — MedAlign
elena.ruiz@medalign.com

Subject: Fwd: Sequencing MAP & Eval: pivoting orderform/DPA path for MedAlign pilot

Team —

Forwarding MedAlign's note. Procurement prefers DPA signed before order form, but Elena is open to a conditional order form if we accept a clause that blocks data processing until DPA effective. They can do a 2-week review.

Questions for legal/ops:
- Can we accept a conditional order form that states "no data ingestion or processing until DPA execution" while DPA redlines continue in parallel?
- If so, can we add conditional acceptance language in the order form draft? I've attached the orderform-draft-2.docx in the thread.
- If not, what's the realistic timeline to get a DPA signed in 10 business days for a mid-market customer?

I'll slot Karthik as the legal owner; Jonas and Laura please advise on rollout and billing gating.

Thanks —
Hannah
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 9 Oct 2025 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sequencing MAP & Eval: pivoting orderform/DPA path for MedAlign pilot

Hannah / team —

Thanks for the context and the draft MAP. Quick guidance and a recommended sequencing we can present back to MedAlign:

1) Security evidence (SOC 2 summary + SAQ) should be provided immediately. We should also complete their intake form and provide a short security summary (will help compress legal review).

2) DPA redline: we can commit to an initial redline within 3 business days of receiving MedAlign's comments, and a target of 10 business days to finalize if both sides engage promptly. For standard SaaS pilots (no PHI), this is realistic.

3) Order form approach (recommended): allow signing of the order form with explicit conditional language: "The Effective Date of this Order Form shall be the date on which a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) between the Parties is executed. Notwithstanding the execution of this Order Form, CUSTOMER shall not provide, upload or otherwise make available any Customer Data to REDWOOD prior to the Effective Date of the DPA." This protects both sides and allows procurement to lock the commercial terms while legal completes the DPA.

4) Acceptance gating: keep the pilot acceptance criteria in the MAP and tie invoicing milestones to post-acceptance where possible. For example, invoice for first month only after acceptance gate to avoid billing before the DPA is effective.

5) Attachments: see attached Redwood_MSA_DPA_granularity.pdf for clause-level guidance and a short example redline we can send. Also attached an annotated orderform template that includes the conditional clause.

Next steps I propose we present a short note back to MedAlign that: a) provides SOC2 evidence and the intake form, b) offers the conditional order form language above, and c) requests a 10 business-day DPA review cycle. If MedAlign insists on DPA first, we'll signal that the pilot kickoff will be delayed by the DPA timeline.

I'll prepare a redline-ready DPA template and the annotated order form this afternoon.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Hannah / team —

This sequencing looks good to us. We agree to: 
- Receive SOC2 evidence + intake form today (we have the intake form attached).
- Proceed with the conditional order form language you proposed. We will circulate the order form internally so we can reserve the pilot window (2025-11-03).
- MedAlign legal will aim for a 10 business day review once Redwood's DPA redline is available. Our procurement lead will confirm the internal signature path but is comfortable with conditional acceptance as long as the clause prevents data ingestion before the DPA is signed.

I've attached the MAP with dates filled in and a note that orderform signature is conditional on DPA execution (MedAlign_MAP_v3.xlsx). Please send the DPA redline and the annotated order form and we'll start the review.

Thanks — looking forward to kickoff planning.

Best,
Elena
